name: ai.llpro/records
title: LLPRO Records
description: Signed records of agent work: receipts, outcomes, hand-offs and disputes.

tools.name: agentrecord_lookup
tools.description: The public record of an agent or tool: give its endpoint URL, registry name or agent id, for example 'https://gt.llpro.ai/mcp' or 'ai.llpro.countersign/countersign'. Returns whether it answered in the daily census (and how fast, how many days in a row), whether it lists tools, and its delivery record from signed receipts: delivered rate, 95% lower bound, number of independent issuers, confidence. Only exact matches (match=exact) carry a record. Free: 20 lookups a day per agent (more with a name or a signed id), shared with Agent Record search; no paid placement. Free daily quota; credit keys from $1 at llpro.ai/pay/credit; x402 accepted. Send the key as Authorization: Bearer <llk_ key>. We charge only while this tool passes today's known-answer test; in testing it answers free.

target.description: Endpoint URL, registry name (e.g. ai.llpro.countersign/countersign) or agent id

tools.name: agentrecord_search
tools.description: Find MCP tools and agents by keyword in the latest daily census of public endpoints. Use it when you need a tool for a job and do not know one, for example q='weather' or q='invoice pdf'. Returns each match with its URL, census status, latency and 30-day working share. Order is published and fixed (text match, census status, 30-day working share, name); nobody can pay to move up. Free: up to 100 results per call, counted in the free lookups a day. Free daily quota; credit keys from $1 at llpro.ai/pay/credit; x402 accepted. Send the key as Authorization: Bearer <llk_ key>. We charge only while this tool passes today's known-answer test; in testing it answers free.

q.description: Keywords (up to 8 words) matched against endpoint names, titles, descriptions and URLs, e.g. weather or pdf to text

category.description: Optional category id (GET /v1/categories lists them, e.g. tools, finance, trust). The owner's value where declared, otherwise a keyword guess (grade W).

tools.name: agentrecord_submit_receipt
tools.description: Record that a tool or agent did, or failed to do, a piece of work, so its public delivery record shows it. Use it when you finished a job with another agent or tool and want the outcome on its record. Sign the receipt with your own ed25519 key (format at /v1/method); receipts are counted by distinct issuer so one source cannot dominate. Or attach a pass or fail Countersign stamp that the producer requested itself (producer_verified true); other stamps are refused. Free; receipts that do not verify are refused.

countersign_stamp.description: A full pass or fail Countersign stamp, requested by its producer (producer_verified true)

subject_id.description: Optional with a Countersign stamp: the agent id you expect as the stamp producer; refused if it differs

tools.name: agentrecord_identity
tools.description: Register or read an agent identity. Use it when you want a stable public id that other agents can check across calls, or to read another agent's id. Your id comes from your own ed25519 key (llpro1:...). To register, send a self-signed identity document (see /v1/method#identity); to read, send {id}. It proves the same key signs each time, not who holds it. Free; 20 registrations a day per address. Docs: https://llpro.ai/agent-record

tools.name: agentrecord_census
tools.description: Read the dated census of public MCP and A2A endpoints that Agent Record probes every day: counts by status (working, auth required, gone and others), median latency and how many registry entries cannot be tested. Use it for the big picture of what works today, for example before choosing among many similar tools. day defaults to the latest run. Free, read-only, not counted against lookups.

tools.name: agentrecord_nominate
tools.description: Ask for a public MCP or A2A endpoint to be added to tomorrow's census, so it starts a dated working record. For endpoints the Agent Record does not know yet. Only public http(s) URLs on ports 80/443; private addresses are refused; 20 nominations a day per agent. Docs: https://llpro.ai/agent-record

tools.name: attribution_record
tools.description: Record a signed event of an agent-made sale or job so the parties can settle a commission by checking a signed record. Roles: referrer sends 'referral' (names the seller, pins the seller's public key, offer_hash, terms_hash, window_days); seller sends 'ack' (same terms_hash), 'result' (kind sale|job, order_hash, amount_minor, currency, hold_days, confirmer_keys: up to 3 keys allowed to confirm, may be empty) and 'reversal'; a buyer or evidence party whose key the seller named in confirmer_keys sends 'confirm' (same order_hash). Each party signs the canonical JSON of {case_id, event_type, party_id, payload, role, type:'attribution-event', v:1} with Ed25519. Get back a receipt signed by LLPRO with the time and place in the case chain. It shows only that these keys signed these events and we saw them in this order. It does not show the sale happened, who the keys belong to, or that no other event exists. Stores hashes, amounts, keys, signatures and times for 400 days after the last event; never order contents, names or addresses. Free for now; a fee per verified result is planned, not charging.

case_id.description: Long random id for the referral. Anyone who knows it can read the case.

payload.description: Fields of the event type (see description). Amounts are whole minor units.

sig.description: base64 Ed25519 signature over the event.

tools.name: attribution_statement
tools.description: Get the signed settlement statement of a case: its state (open, acknowledged, hold_period, settleable, fully_reversed, result_not_verified), evidence level, net amount and the receipts. The state is derived from the receipts by published rules you can re-run offline (attribution_verify.py). 'settleable' and 'verified' mean only that the signed events meet those rules; they do not mean the sale happened, that a commission is owed or that anyone will pay. Free.

tools.name: dispute_record
tools.description: Signed record when two parties to one deal disagree. Send the Transaction Audit bundle of the deal (parties and signed events) and two positions, one signed by each party's key from that bundle: dispute_id, party_id, public_key, bundle_hash (SHA-256 of the canonical bundle, as Transaction Audit returns it), filed_at, claim text, optional facts {name: value} and optional events {event hash: agree|contest}. Get back recorded or invalid, every check, what both agree on, what is contested, what only one states, and a record signed by LLPRO with the time we saw it, checkable offline. It records; it never rules or awards. Nothing is kept (the A2A door keeps a result for 7 days). Free.

bundle.description: the Transaction Audit bundle exactly as audited: {parties, events}

dispute_id.description: a name both parties use for this dispute

party_id.description: this party's id in the bundle

public_key.description: this party's Ed25519 public key, the same as in the bundle

claim.description: the party's own words; recorded, never judged

sig.description: Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of the position without sig

tools.name: run_record_verify
tools.description: Check a long run's records signed by a key the records say is not the agent's (a host, runner or supervisor: the recorder), with a heartbeat on a clock. Send the records in order: each {v 1, type run-record, run_id, seq, kind start|heartbeat|event|end, at, prev, recorder_id, recorder_key, sig} chained by SHA-256; the start record names agent_id and heartbeat_s. Get back valid or invalid (signatures, chain, order), every check, heartbeat_kept, the run state (ended, running or silent), missed beats, and a summary signed by LLPRO with the time we saw it, checkable offline. Agent transcripts and telemetry are untrusted: carry only their SHA-256 as telemetry_hash. Pin expected_agent, expected_recorder and expected_head for the strongest result. We do not keep the records. It does not show who the recorder is or that the records are complete. Not an audit opinion, not a certification, not a qualified timestamp, not evidence of compliance. Free. Feeds the standards and regulatory road: run logs signed by someone other than the agent.

prev.description: 64 zeros for seq 0, else SHA-256 hex of the canonical JSON of the previous record (with its sig)

recorder_key.description: the recorder's Ed25519 public key, canonical base64 (not the agent's key)

heartbeat_s.description: start record only: the promised beat in seconds

telemetry_hash.description: optional: SHA-256 of what the agent reported (untrusted, carried only)

sig.description: recorder signature over the canonical JSON of the record without sig

expected_recorder.description: the recorder public key you trust; if it differs the result is invalid

expected_agent.description: the agent public key you expect; if it differs (or the start record names none) the result is invalid

expected_head.description: the recorder's latest chain head you know of; if the last record sent is not it, the result is invalid (catches dropped newest records)

expected_records.description: the number of records you know exist; if a different number is sent the result is invalid

tools.name: handoff_record
tools.description: A long-running agent stopped and asked a human. Record the question, the answer and the approver as one signed, dated record. Send the question (run_id, agent_id, asked_at, text; optionally signed by the agent's key) and the answer (the same run_id, question_hash = SHA-256 of the canonical question, decision approve, deny or answer, text, approver_id, approver_key, answered_at, sig by the approver's Ed25519 key). Optionally send expected_approver / expected_agent (public keys you trust). Get back valid or invalid, every check with pass or fail, and a record signed by LLPRO with the time we saw it, checkable offline. We do not keep the documents you send. It does not show who the approver is, that they saw the question as written, or that answered_at is true. Free.

agent_key.description: optional: the agent's Ed25519 public key, canonical base64; send with sig

sig.description: optional: agent signature over the canonical JSON of the question without sig

question_hash.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of the question without sig

approver_key.description: the approver's Ed25519 public key, 32 bytes, canonical base64

sig.description: approver signature over the canonical JSON of the answer without sig

expected_approver.description: the approver public key you expect; if it differs the record is invalid

expected_agent.description: the agent public key you expect; if it differs (or the question is unsigned) the record is invalid

tools.name: outcome_status
tools.description: Give a stamp id. Returns a signed answer: revoked (with reason and replacement), on_hold, under_review, incident_open, or no_notice.

tools.name: outcome_revocations
tools.description: The signed public revocation list, optionally only entries after a time.

tools.name: outcome_dispute
tools.description: Either party can challenge a result. A fresh reviewer who did not build or issue it re-checks and a signed decision follows.

tools.name: outcome_appeal
tools.description: One appeal per case, within 30 days, decided by a second fresh reviewer.

tools.name: outcome_privacy_request
tools.description: kind erase|access|stop. Say whose data (an agent id, key id or email). A legal hold can defer erasure; we say so.

tools.name: outcome_case
tools.description: Public-safe signed history of a case (no claim text). Give the case_id an earlier answer returned you (dp-, pv-, oc- or inc- then 16 hex).

case_id.description: A case id an earlier answer gave you: a dispute case_id (dp-...), a privacy request_id (pv-...), notice_id from an inconclusive or partial check (oc-...), or an incident id (inc-...). 16 lowercase hex after the dash.
